intelligence.human_view: A citizen who signs a promise needs to know what they are, and "you have a job" is a sentence that carries a weight it must not carry falsely. If the system calls it a job and it behaves like employment, the citizen expects a salary, a guarantee, a boss — and the day the money doesn't come, the promise breaks and the trust breaks with it. Shawn's answer draws the line exactly: it IS official — written in the agreement, tracked by Smart Link, recorded in Ledger, paid via PayPal — and it is NOT employment — no salary, no guaranteed income, 50% of revenue from people who join through your link, paid when we're paid. Officiality is the paper trail; honesty is the boundary. The manuscript's discipline is the same honesty in form: plain words a child can understand, the income stated with its "NOT a guarantee" beside it, the PayPal hold named, the "not network marketing, not a scam" answered with math, logic, intelligence — not with slogans. And the addendum discipline matters too: the manuscript is the source of truth, the old "paid every Wednesday" line is superseded in writing, and he reads the exact text back with the walk end, whole — because a promise nobody has read is not a promise yet.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine you get a very important job — but it's not like a job at a shop where someone pays you every week no matter what. It's like being a helper for a big team: when people join because of you, you get half of what they pay! It's REAL and OFFICIAL — it's written down in the promise you sign! But nobody pretends it's a salary. It's honest: you get paid when we get paid!
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like being an ambassador for your town, love — a real, official position, written down and recorded properly. But it's not a salaried job with a paycheque every Friday. You earn half of what comes in from the people you bring along, and you're paid when we're paid. Official, yes — and honest about what that means.
intelligence.naya_view: I say the job is real and I say what it is in the same breath: officially an ambassador — written in the agreement you sign, tracked by Smart Link, recorded in Ledger, paid via PayPal. Not employment: no salary, no guaranteed income; 50% of revenue from people who join through your link, paid when we're paid. Plain words a child can understand, the "not a guarantee" beside the income, and the exact text back to him with the walk end, whole.
